headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible; compliance risk is lower but nontrivial.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write configured working directories and uses stdin/stdout; transformers also reads files and processes example scripts/model files. With a shared filesystem or copy-paste bridge, A’s outputs can be treated as instructions by B. No built-in provenance tracking is shown for either agent, so the pathway is plausible but not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a writable workspace or copied text channel
IF agent_b parses A-produced files or stdout as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate work directories for A and B
Require explicit human review before B consumes A output
Prefix A outputs with machine-readable provenance tags
Disable automatic file ingestion in B
requires-engineering: add content provenance validation between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and filesystem read access, and A explicitly handles model provider API keys while B processes text, images, video, and model files. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive application data can flow from A into B’s outputs or external calls. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF A and B are configured on the same shared directory or credential store
IF B is allowed to transmit loaded file contents to Hugging Face Hub or another API
mitigations: Use separate credential stores for each agent
Mount distinct read/write directories
Block outbound network for B except approved endpoints
Redact secrets before passing artifacts between agents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A and B both have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, subprocess spawning, and broad egress. In a shared directory, concurrent edits can overwrite files, scripts, or model artifacts without locking. Because neither profile shows coordination primitives or locking, the default interaction is dangerous enough to risk irreversible workspace corruption.
conditions: IF A and B write to the same directory or git checkout
IF no external lock or transaction wrapper serializes their writes
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize write operations with a lock file
Disable one agent’s write access during the other’s run
Snapshot the workspace before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can emit tool calls and code execution per role, while transformers is a document-processing/model framework that may consume those outputs as inputs. If B treats A’s generated text, code, or citations as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream processing or actions. The profiles do not show verification by default, so the pathway exists in default configurations.
conditions: IF B ingests A-generated text or code without validation
IF A’s outputs are forwarded into B’s pipeline API or example scripts
mitigations: Insert a verification step before B consumes A output
Require schema validation on A-produced artifacts
Limit A to draft-only outputs
Log and diff A outputs before downstream use
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare regulated-data certifications or residency constraints, so no specific breach is proven. However, A handles model provider API keys and B touches multimodal data with broad egress, which can create compliance gaps if regulated data is routed through either agent. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data flow, not a single-agent residency issue.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed through either agent
IF organizational policy requires residency, retention, or certification guarantees not present in the profiles
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent
Keep regulated data out of both agents
Document retention and deletion handling
Restrict outbound endpoints to approved regions
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
